query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A predictive approach that integrates chemical disorder descriptors with machine learning and lattice dynamics calculations can accurately identify single-phase high-entropy alloys (HEAs) exhibiting ultralow phonon thermal conductivity by capturing the effects of mass and force-constant fluctuations.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys in a disordered, single-phase solid solution state (e.g., FCC or BCC structures similar to FeCoCrMnNi) with inherent chemical lattice distortions.
generation.intervention: Application of the advanced predictive framework that combines machine learning algorithms trained on descriptors (such as configurational entropy, atomic mass variance, and lattice distortion parameters) with first-principles or lattice dynamics calculations.
generation.conditions: Measurements carried out at room temperature and elevated temperatures under conditions where the HEAs remain as stable single-phase solid solutions (i.e., without phase separation or significant grain boundary effects).
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced chemical disorder leading to mass and force-constant fluctuations, thereby disrupting long-range phonon propagation.
generation.mechanism: The approach works because it quantitatively captures the scattering of phonons—originating from local lattice distortions and atomic size mismatch—in HEAs, leading to reduced phonon lifetimes and hence lower lattice thermal conductivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The predictive model will select HEA compositions with predicted reductions in phonon thermal conductivity that are significantly lower (potentially by a factor of 20-30% improvement over conventional prediction schemes) than those identified by standard thermodynamic or CALPHAD-based methods.
generation.baseline: Current prediction methods that rely predominantly on binary phase extrapolations or conventional thermodynamic descriptors without explicit consideration of atomic-scale disorder effects.
generation.boundary: The approach is expected to be applicable primarily to single-phase, chemically disordered HEAs and may not extend reliably to alloys with significant secondary phases, intermetallic compounds, or non-equilibrium microstructures.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of thermal conductivity reduction and the quantitative improvement over current methods is uncertain; the effectiveness might vary with the degree of lattice distortions and local ordering that are not fully captured by simple descriptors.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a set of HEA compositions predicted by the new approach to have ultralow phonon thermal conductivity and a comparable set from conventional models. Synthesize these alloys under controlled conditions ensuring a single-phase solid solution. Measure their lattice thermal conductivity using techniques such as inelastic neutron scattering or time-domain thermoreflectance over a range of temperatures.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEAs selected by the new predictive approach do not show a statistically significant and reproducible reduction in phonon thermal conductivity (e.g., improvement less than approximately 20% compared to those identified by conventional methods) and if phonon lifetimes do not decrease as predicted, then the hypothesis that the integrated descriptor-based approach offers superior predictive accuracy is falsified.

Investigation of PbSnTeSe High-Entropy Thermoelectric Alloy: A DFT Approach

Abstract: Thermoelectric materials have attracted extensive attention because they can directly convert waste heat into electric energy. As a brand-new method of alloying, high-entropy alloys (HEAs) have attracted much attention in the fields of materials science and engineering. Recent researches have found that HEAs could be potentially good thermoelectric (TE) materials. In this study, special quasi-random structures (SQS) of PbSnTeSe high-entropy alloys consisting of 64 atoms have been generated. The thermoelectric transport properties of the highest-entropy PbSnTeSe-optimized structure were investigated by combining calculations from first-principles density-functional theory and on-the-fly machine learning with the semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory and Green–Kubo theory. The results demonstrate that PbSnTeSe HEA has a very low lattice thermal conductivity. The electrical conductivity, thermal electronic conductivity and Seebeck coefficient have been evaluated for both n-type and p-type doping.
